display.title: Nissan, the Month of Miracles: Seeing Hashem in Nature
display.summary_short: The name Nissan comes from 'neis', a miracle. Uncle Yossi explains the miracles of the Exodus and why nature itself is the greatest miracle of all.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given just before Rosh Chodesh Nissan. Uncle Yossi explains that one reason the month is called Nissan is that its letters nun and samech spell 'neis', a miracle. He describes the miracles of the Exodus: the Ten Plagues and the splitting of the Yam Suf, where, as the Midrash relates, the seabed was carpeted with soft grass, springs of drink flowed from the walls of water and colorful birds sang overhead. But a Jew does not need miracles to know that Hashem created the world. The rising sun, the stars at night and trees that give fruit are all acts of Hashem; the only difference between nature and a miracle is how often it happens, and nature is really the greatest miracle. As the Navi says, 'Lift up your eyes and see who created these.' Strong emunah will bring the greatest miracle of all, the coming of Moshiach, and just as the first redemption came in Nissan, so will the last.
display.lesson: Look at the world around you: nature itself is Hashem's miracle, and seeing it strengthens our emunah.
